statement: Nebius raising on-demand rental prices for a second time in 2026 points to rentable GPU capacity staying scarce rather than slack building up in the chain.
why: A neocloud can only push list prices up twice in one year if utilization is high and customers have few cheaper alternatives, which says the chain is not carrying idle capacity.

impact.mechanism: Tight rentable capacity keeps utilization and pricing high for existing fleets, which supports continued accelerator purchases to add capacity.

evidence.excerpt: may increase or decrease based on available capacity, cluster utilization, customer demand
reports this October hike as the second increase in the year: the first hike, reported around May 2026, raised on-demand H100 rental from $2.95/hour to $3.85/hour (about a 29% jump)

reasoning: Two list-price increases inside one calendar year, on a page that ties spot pricing to available capacity and cluster utilization, is consistent with demand running ahead of deployable supply; the document offers no utilization figure, so this stays an inference rather than a measurement.

confidence.basis: Inference from a vendor price page plus search-summarized coverage of the earlier hike; no utilization or occupancy data in the document.
